sub: Named after “competing for more” (at-takāthur) in ayah 1
theme: The race for more wealth, children and status distracts people until they die. They will see Hell with their own eyes and be asked about every pleasure they enjoyed.
story: Usually counted as a very early Makkan surah, though some reports link it to Madinah.

Reportedly it came about two clans who boasted over which had more leaders and men. After counting the living, they went to the graveyards and counted their dead. Other reports name the Jews, a clan of the Anṣār, or traders; its words cover them all.
The Prophet ﷺ recited it and said: “The son of Adam says, ‘My wealth, my wealth!’ But what do you really have of it, except what you ate and used up, wore out, or gave in charity?”

sections.title: Distracted until the grave
sections.meaning: The race for more (wealth, children, followers, status) keeps you busy until you end up in the graves. No! You will soon know. Then again, no! You will soon know.
points: No! You will know. Then no! You will know.
sections.matters: It names a sickness of every age: chasing more until death ends the chase. The grave is called a visit, not a home, because it is a stop on the way to the lasting home.
sections.story: Reportedly about two clans boasting of their numbers. When the living were counted, they went to the graveyard to count their dead. Other reports name different groups, and the words fit them all.
explained: Alhākum at-takāthur: the race for more has pulled you away from worshipping Allah. What is raced for is not named, so it covers wealth, children, supporters, rank, anything used to outdo others. It lasts ḥattā zurtum al-maqābir: until you die and are buried. If the son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would want a second.

Kallā: stop, more is not the point. Sawfa taʿlamūn: you will know. It is said twice, a warning after a warning: you will know at death and then in the grave, or in the grave and then at the resurrection. Some Companions said they had doubted the punishment of the grave until this surah came.
teaches: Ask yourself what your busyness is distracting you from.
You keep only what you eat, wear out or give away.
The grave is a stop, not the final home.
Greed and hope stay young even when a person grows old.
sections.hook: Ayah 4 repeats ayah 3 word for word (kallā sawfa taʿlamūn), adding only thumma (“then”) at the start.

sections.title: You will see it, and be asked
sections.meaning: No! If you knew with certain knowledge, the race for more would never have distracted you. You will surely see Hellfire. Then you will see it with the eye of certainty. Then you will be asked that Day about every pleasure.
points: If only you knew with ʿilm al-yaqīn
Then you will see it with ʿayn al-yaqīn
Then you will be asked about every pleasure
sections.matters: Knowing about the Hereafter is not the same as being certain of it; real certainty changes how people live. And every blessing, even cool shade, fresh dates and cool water, will be asked about.
sections.story: When ayah 8 came, people reportedly asked what pleasures they had, with only dates and water and the enemy close. The Prophet ﷺ said: “That will come.”
explained: Kallā law taʿlamūna ʿilm al-yaqīn: if you knew with a knowledge that reaches the heart, the race for more would never have distracted you, and you would hurry to good deeds. The end of the sentence is left unsaid, for effect.

Then comes sight. You will see al-jaḥīm, then see it ʿayn al-yaqīn, with your own eyes, the highest certainty. Then you will be asked about an-naʿīm: health, free time, safety, food and drink. Did you thank Allah and give His right in it, or use it to disobey Him?
teaches: Knowledge that reaches the heart changes how you live.
Don’t wait to see the Fire before you believe in it.
Health and free time are blessings many people waste.
Thank Allah for every pleasure; each one will be asked about.
sections.hook: Yaqīn ends ayah 5 and ayah 7: ʿilm al-yaqīn, then ʿayn al-yaqīn. La-tarawunna opens ayah 6 and returns in ayah 7, and thumma opens ayat 7 and 8.

groups.text: The race for more wealth, children and status keeps you distracted until you are buried.
No! You will soon know where it leads. Then no! You will soon know.
If you truly knew with certainty, you would not be distracted. You will surely see Hellfire.
You will see it with your own eyes, then be asked about every pleasure you enjoyed.

1.explain: Alhākum: kept you busy, away from obeying Allah. At-takāthur: competing to have more and boasting of it. What is competed in is left unnamed, so it covers wealth, children, followers and rank.
1.why: Reportedly about two clans of Quraysh, Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm, boasting over who had more leaders and men. Other reports say the Jews, a clan of the Anṣār, or traders.

2.explain: Zurtum al-maqābir: you visited the graves, meaning you died and were buried. A visitor does not stay; the grave leads on to the lasting home. Another view: until you counted your dead to win.
2.why: In the clan report, after the living were counted, they went to the graveyards and counted graves by name, and Banū Sahm came out ahead.

3.explain: Kallā: stop, it is not about having more. Sawfa taʿlamūn: you will soon know the bad end of your boasting. Some Companions said this surah ended their doubts about the punishment of the grave.

4.explain: Repeated with thumma (“then”): a warning after a warning. Either you will know at death and then in the grave, or in the grave and then in the Hereafter.

5.explain: ʿIlm al-yaqīn: certain knowledge. If you truly knew what is ahead, you would not be distracted. The rest of the sentence is left unsaid, for effect.

6.explain: La-tarawunna al-jaḥīm: you will surely see the blazing Fire. The form carries an oath: this is certain.

7.explain: ʿAyn al-yaqīn: the eye of certainty, seeing it for yourself. Seeing with your own eyes is the highest certainty, above knowing by report.

8.explain: An-naʿīm: every pleasure (health, free time, safety, food, drink). Either all are asked, as good news for the believer and rebuke for the disbeliever, or in one view only disbelievers.
8.why: When it came down, people reportedly asked: “Which pleasures? We have only dates and water, the enemy is near, and our swords are on our shoulders.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “That will come.”
